claims.title: Decode represented qLTC syndromes and state the missing energy-to-computation interface

quoted_fields.interface: Fixed binary CSS family identified by the supplied2609.20780v1 source, with its ACTUAL face, stalk, incidence, field-basis and compatible-chart representation supplied. The decoder receives exact noiseless binary syndromes of promised sufficiently small Pauli errors; it does not reconstruct this representation from arbitrary sparse parity-check matrices. Energy statements require H_code>=sigma D_C/N. The gap lemma separately requires A>=g(I-P), 0<=B<=I and PBP>=beta P with g,beta>0; an actual robust bounded-locality computation test B is NOT supplied. Transport requires an explicitly supplied physical unitary with forward AND backward support expansion<=ell.
quoted_fields.failure: No construction of a robust local computation test satisfying P_r B P_r>=beta P_r on every physical NO-state; no complete charged arithmetic-tower construction from an arbitrary QMA instance. Clean syndrome decoding is not noisy-syndrome handling, adversarial fault-tolerant computation or a local coherent verification relation. Reference-safe correction is warranted for genuine error channels with Kraus operators in the low-weight Pauli span; decoding an arbitrary low-distance vector does not identify a prior intended logical state. Logical changes inside the codespace have zero code energy, so code energy does not impose initialization, propagation or rejection. The adversarial-computation guarantee f(N)=2^-O(sqrt(log N)) remains vanishing, includes its noiseless classical-function/logical-postselection qualifications, and supplies no proved circuit-to-Hamiltonian correspondence. Average code energy e over L frames gives only Pr(any bad frame)<=Le/g; a constant per-time fault guarantee is not established.
